title: Choose the layout after the ring
question: Schedule and drawing set kept; the letter is replaced. Which structure should carry the case study, the service picker, the estimate and the emailed plan?

options.label: Your site on the workbench
options.lineage: a craftsman's bench with parts laid out beside the frame
options.thesis: The hero frame returns as the visitor's own site in wireframe, and each service they pick drops in and turns solid.
materials: service parts laid in a tray
solid gold hairline when a part is placed
options.viewport: A large dashed site wireframe on the left (nav, booking box, payment slot, language switch); a tray of service parts on the right; the estimate sits under the frame and grows with each part.
options.risk: Needs one wireframe slot per service; ideas the visitor types have no slot and go to a notes strip.

options.label: The drawing set
options.lineage: architect's numbered drawing sheets with a title block
options.thesis: The hero's wireframe-to-built idea continues: every section is a drawing sheet, and choosing a service builds it on the plan.
materials: dashed modules that turn solid when chosen
a title block that collects the plan
options.viewport: Sheet A: the case study with screens and dimension lines. Sheet B: services drawn as dashed rooms of a site plan; ticking one draws it solid, and the corner title block totals the weeks.
options.risk: Can tip into an architecture costume if the drawing devices outnumber the content.

options.label: The schedule
options.lineage: a production schedule ruled in weeks
options.thesis: The service picker is the delivery timeline itself: each ticked service draws its bar, and the finish line moves.
materials: a week ruler across the page
gold bars that draw on selection
options.viewport: Case study as a wide pinned screen strip; then a full-width week ruler with one row per service, checkbox at left, and the finish marker reading the total weeks.
options.risk: Rows of bars can read like project-management software if the type is not kept large.
